rv.q: In a show all about uncertainty, one thing is certain: in Only Human , Brown is at his astounding best.
It’s a thoroughly entertaining, at times mind-warping exploration of how magical we still find the idea of being able to predict the future, five centuries after Nostradamus.
Brown is a master of his craft and Only Human reminds us that he really is one of the greatest showmen of them all.
For that alone, he deserves our respect and applause.
In this brand-new production, Derren Brown combines mind-reading, psychological illusion, and breathtaking storytelling in a way that is both deeply personal and utterly electrifying.
Only Human is an electrifying piece of theatre on the comedy and curiosity within our contradictions.
This is a slick, fast-paced spectacle that will have you slack-jawed throughout.
Brown once again demonstrates why he remains in a league of his own.
Yet while the individual tricks may intrigue, what’s noticeably absent is the storytelling that has often bound his previous shows together.

cn.t: Brown's latest mind-bending showcase dazzles most critics with electrifying illusions and slick showmanship, though some find it lacks the human connection its title promises. A mesmerizing return to form that keeps audiences guessing.
